statement.p: Parameterize a vase formed by rotating the curve z= 6 \sqrt{x-2},\,2\leq x\leq 4, around the z-axis. Use s and t for your parameters.

static.solution:
z=6\sqrt{x-2}, 2\le x\le 4, around the z-axis is shown in the figure below.
At height z, the cross-section is a horizontal circle of radius a. Thus, letting the angle \theta around the z-axis be t, a point on this horizontal circle is given by \vec r=a \cos t \vec i + a \sin t \vec j + z\vec k. However, the radius a and height z are not independent. We can parameterize easily in two ways: first, suppose that we take the radius a to be our second parameter, a = s. Then, the height z = 6\sqrt{s - 2}, and our parameterization is x(s,t) = s\cos t, y(s,t) = s\sin t, and z(s,t) = 6\sqrt{s - 2}, with 2\le s\le 4 \quad\mbox{and}\quad 0\le t\le 2\pi. Alternately, we could take the height z to be the second parameter, z = s. Then, solving for the radius r in the expression for the curve, we get a = \left(\frac{s}{6}\right)^2 + 2. Thus in this case the parameterization is x(s,t) = \left((\frac{s}{6})^2 + 2\right)\,\cos(t), y(s,t) = \left((\frac{s}{6})^2 + 2\right)\,\sin(t), and z(s,t) = s, with 0\le s\le 6\sqrt{2}\quad\mbox{and}\quad 0\le t\le 2\pi.
